question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Tick the right answer
question_types.how: The answer is one of the printed options; the engine compares the option ticked with the key.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Match each one to its partner
question_types.how: Each line drawn is a pair; the engine compares every pair with the key.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Number them in order
question_types.how: The numbers written are an order; the engine compares the order with the key, which code computes where it can (alphabetical order, the order of events in the passage).

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Write each one in the right group
question_types.how: Each item belongs to one group; the engine compares every item's group with the key.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Fill the gap
question_types.how: One word or a short phrase in a gap; the engine compares it with the key and the list of accepted answers, spelling exact.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Write the word
question_types.how: One written word; the engine compares the spelling letter by letter with the key, which code computes from the rule where it can.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Listen and write
question_types.how: The educator reads a word or sentence aloud from the paper's list; the child writes it; the engine compares the spelling letter by letter with the key.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Underline or circle the words
question_types.how: The words underlined are a set; the engine compares the set with the key: every target word, and no other.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Copy the words from the passage
question_types.how: The words copied must be in the passage; the engine compares them with the key and accepted answers, ignoring case and end punctuation.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Write it again with the punctuation
question_types.how: The sentence written again; the engine checks that its words are unchanged and that every mark is in its place.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Find and fix the mistakes
question_types.how: The corrected words; the engine compares each correction with the key and counts a correct word changed as a new mistake.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Complete the table
question_types.how: One fact per box; the engine compares each box with the key and its accepted answers.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Answer in a sentence or two
question_types.how: A short written answer with more than one right wording; a person reads every answer against the question's key points and the rubric while the kind is new.
question_types.first_answers: every answer seen by a person

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Write the sentence again so that it does what is asked
question_types.how: The rewritten sentence, with more than one right wording; code checks what it can (the asked-for word or mark is there), and a person reads every answer while the kind is new.
question_types.first_answers: every answer seen by a person

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Write a short piece
question_types.how: Three to eight sentences of the child's own; a person reads every answer and gives a level for each line of the rubric while the kind is new.
question_types.first_answers: every answer seen by a person

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Read aloud to the educator
question_types.how: Not on a paper: the educator listens and records what they saw against the objective.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Talk, listen and discuss
question_types.how: Not on a paper: the educator watches talk, discussion or performance and records what they saw.

question_types.subject: ENG
question_types.name: Extended writing in the exercise book
question_types.how: Not on a paper: a full piece written over a lesson or more, judged by the educator across the term.
